candidates.title: Palazzo Altemps and Baths of Diocletian museum
candidates.summary: Two parts of the Museo Nazionale Romano close together, with Roman sculpture in a Renaissance palazzo with a courtyard and the great baths complex. Gentle indoor visits with seating; I could not confirm handrails on every staircase, so check lifts and ramps before going.

candidates.title: Galleria Borghese Caravaggio and Bernini rooms
candidates.summary: A compact villa museum with Caravaggio, Bernini and Titian, ideal for a slow Baroque morning. Entry is by timed ticket, so book ahead; the gardens outside are mostly flat, but I could not check gravel paths.

candidates.title: Campo de' Fiori and Testaccio market browse
candidates.summary: Browse food stalls at a relaxed pace and stop for coffee. Campo de' Fiori is cobbled, so Testaccio's covered market may suit the walking limit better; I do not know the current opening days.

candidates.title: Capitoline Museums: Palazzo Nuovo and Pinacoteca
candidates.summary: Roman sculpture, the Capitoline Wolf, and Baroque paintings by Caravaggio and Guercino in one place. It has lifts and a café terrace; the piazza is partly cobbled, so take a taxi to the door.

candidates.title: Ostia Antica self-guided ruins visit
candidates.summary: A well-preserved Roman port town, less crowded than the Forum, with a theatre and mosaics. Paths are uneven in places with some ancient paving, so keep to the main road and rest often; I could not account for the surfaces at the time of your visit.

candidates.title: Santa Maria del Popolo Caravaggio chapel
candidates.summary: A quiet church visit to see two Caravaggio paintings in the Cerasi Chapel, with Bernini works nearby. It is free to enter; opening hours around services vary, so check them on the day.

candidates.title: Museo dell'Ara Pacis
candidates.summary: The Augustan altar of peace in a bright modern building, flat and easy to walk, with seating. A calm single-subject visit that suits a slow morning.

candidates.title: Galleria Doria Pamphilj
candidates.summary: A private palace gallery with Caravaggio, Velázquez and Titian, and an audio guide included. It is a gentle indoor visit, though I could not check the handrails in the older stairways.
